Where to Stay on Koh Kood?
12 Real-Reviewed Hotels

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Koh Kood hotels across every level — 4-star pool villas and beachfront resorts down to garden bungalows and great-value hostels, spread across the main bays Klong Chao, Bang Bao, Ao Tapao and Ao Phrao. From ฿1,200–7,000/night.
heroStats: 🏖️ Several main bays (Klong Chao·Bang Bao·Ao Tapao·Ao Phrao)
introH2: 🏝️ Why does choosing the right bay on Koh Kood matter so much?
introHtml: Koh Kood is Thailand's fourth-largest island, way out at the far end of the Trat sea near the Cambodian border, and still quieter and more unspoiled than many famous islands — but each bay is far apart and has a distinctly different feel. Klong Chao is the popular long white-sand beach with a kayak-able canal and the most places to stay and eat. Bang Bao is a clear-water curved bay in the south, quiet and pretty. Ao Tapao is a calm hilltop with sea views, good for couples. Ao Phrao and Klong Mad are quiet private-beach zones, while Ao Ngamkho sits mid-island for easy access. Plenty of people book without checking which bay and then end up chartering a songthaew or hopping boats between bays all day, losing time and money. This guide rounds up 12 hand-picked Koh Kood hotels we've read real reviews for, across every level — from pool villas and beachfront resorts to garden bungalows and hostels — each with a 3-site price compare and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Koh Kood has no public transport. Getting around the island means renting a scooter, chartering a songthaew, or using your resort's shuttle — some stretches of road climb steep hills. To reach the island, take a speedboat from Laem Sok / Laem Ngop pier in Trat, about 1–1.5 hours (some resorts run their own boat). Main bays in this guide: Klong Chao — popular long white-sand beach, kayak canal, lots of stays (Tinkerbell, Tolani, Peter Pan, Little White Bird) · Bang Bao — clear-water curved bay in the south (The Beach Natural) · Ao Tapao — calm hilltop with sea views (Shantaa) · Klong Mad — private beach on a hill (Koh Kood Beach Resort, Koh Kood Garden) · Ao Phrao — shallow-water beach at the south tip (Rest Sea, Ao Phrao Beach Resort) · Ao Ngamkho and Klong Rahan (Secret Beach) — mid-island / hidden beaches (Dusita, Captain Hook).

entries.name: Shantaa Koh Kood

rooms.type: Shantaa Extra Sweet PLUS (up to 4 guests)

entries.addr: Ao Tapao, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Shantaa is the most-reviewed hotel on Koh Kood — 385 reviews at 9.4. Villas are spread across a hillside above Ao Tapao, each one private, looking out over the sea and the sunset. Reviews most often praise the calm couples-friendly feel, the semi-open bathrooms, and a breakfast many say is made fresh and tasty. There are free kayaks and surfboards to borrow — a fit for anyone who wants a quiet rest rather than being right on the sand.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The villas are on a hill with steps; if walking up is hard, ask for a lower-level unit. Many Koh Kood places close in low season (May–Oct), so check the open dates before you book.
pros: Most reviewed on the island — 385 reviews at 9.4
Hilltop sea-view villas, private and quiet
Fresh breakfast, often praised in reviews
Free kayaks and surfboards to borrow
cons: Hilltop villas mean stairs — not ideal if walking is hard
Not directly on the beach — you walk down to the sand

entries.name: Tinkerbell Privacy Resort

rooms.type: Beach Front Villa (step out to the sand)

entries.addr: 116 Moo 2, Baan Klong Chao, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Tinkerbell is a beachfront villa resort on Klong Chao and the island's second-most reviewed — 181 reviews at 9.1. With just 15 villas it feels private, and the beachfront villas open their folding doors straight onto the sand. It sits on Klong Chao, the island's most popular beach with white sand, clear water and a kayak-able canal nearby — a premium pick for anyone who wants to sleep right by the sea in an area with restaurants and activities close by.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For true beachfront pick a Beach Front Villa — there are only 8 and they sell out fast, so book ahead. The Standard rooms are cheaper but not in the front row by the sand.
pros: Beachfront villas open straight onto the sand
Well reviewed — 181 reviews at 9.1 on a popular beach
Small resort, only 15 villas — private
Klong Chao has white sand, clear water and great sunsets
cons: Above the island average on price, especially beachfront villas
Front-row beachfront rooms are limited and sell out fast in high season

entries.name: Koh Kood Beach Resort
entries.addr: 121 Moo 1, Klong Mad, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Koh Kood Beach Resort is the highest-scoring resort in this 3-star group at 9.5 — thatched Bali-style bungalows spread across a hill above a private bay in the Klong Mad area. The standouts are the sea-view infinity pool and the quiet private beach. Each bungalow is around 46 sqm with an open-air bathroom. There are free kayaks and bikes, and from just ฿2,400 it's great value for a private-beach resort on Koh Kood.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pay a little more for a Bali House sea view — the sunset view from the terrace is well worth it. The bungalows are on a hill with some up-and-down, so pack comfortable shoes.
pros: Highest score in the 3-star group at 9.5
Sea-view infinity pool and a quiet private beach
Bali bungalows around 46 sqm, great starting price
Free kayaks and bikes to borrow
cons: Bungalows are on a hill — not ideal if walking is hard
Open-air Bali-style bathrooms may not suit everyone

entries.name: Dusita Resort Kohkood
entries.addr: Ao Ngamkho Beach, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Dusita is the highest-scoring stay on Koh Kood — 9.7 from 150 reviews — even though it's a simple 2-star garden bungalow place. The reason the score is this high is the owner and staff, whom reviews mention again and again for their warmth and care, plus a fresh, tasty breakfast. It sits on Ao Ngamkho beach mid-island, so it's easy to reach the other bays, with both budget fan rooms and air-con family bungalows — a fit for anyone who values warm service over polish.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The fan rooms are the cheapest, and Koh Kood nights are pleasantly cool anyway. If you're a group, the Triple or Family Bungalow is better value — and book direct with the resort to ask about boat transfers.
pros: Highest score on the island — 9.7 from 150 reviews
Warm, hands-on owner and staff, often praised in reviews
Fresh breakfast · friendly starting price
Mid-island location, easy to reach the other bays
cons: It's a simple 2-star bungalow place, not a luxury resort
The budget rooms are fan-only, no air-con

entries.name: Peter Pan Resort
entries.badge: 🌅 Where the canal meets the sea
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Klong Chao beach (canal mouth) · Koh Kood
entries.addr: 102 Moo 2, Baan Klong Chao, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Peter Pan Resort sits right where Klong Chao canal flows out to meet the sea on Klong Chao beach, scoring 9.1 from 75 reviews. The beachfront bungalows are an easy step from the sand, and reviews love the friendly vibe, free ice cream, an evening fire show and a great sunset spot. It's on Klong Chao with restaurants and the kayak launch close by — a fit for anyone who wants to sleep on a popular beach for less than a 4-star villa.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Mermaid garden-view room is the cheapest but not on the beach; for a sea view pick the Sea Horse. Kayaking up the canal in the morning, when the water is calmest, is a must-do.
pros: Right at the Klong Chao canal mouth on a popular beach
Friendly vibe, free ice cream, fire show
Great sunset spot, free kayaks to borrow
More affordable than the 4-star villas in the same area
cons: The starting room is garden view, not on the beach
A 3-star resort — facilities aren't as plush as the villas

entries.name: The Beach Natural Resort

rooms.type: Beach Villa (by the sea, 5–10 m from beach)

entries.addr: Bang Bao Bay, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: The Beach Natural Resort sits on Bang Bao, a clear-water curved bay in the south of the island that's both pretty and quiet, scoring 8.9 from 37 reviews. It has Bali-style garden cottages, beach villas by the sea, and even two-bedroom pool villas for families. The standout is the private wooden jetty reaching out into the bay and a back-to-nature feel, with free kayaks — a fit for a quiet beachfront rest away from the bustle of Klong Chao.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The starting Natural Cottage is in the garden, 50–80 m from the beach; for true beachfront you'll need a Beach Villa. Bang Bao is in the south, far from Klong Chao, so allow travel time on the island.
pros: On clear-water Bang Bao bay — quiet and pretty
Private wooden jetty into the bay, back-to-nature feel
Range of rooms from cottage to family pool villa
Free kayaks to borrow
cons: High starting price, and the entry room is in the garden, not on the beach
Bang Bao is far from Klong Chao — long travel around the island

entries.type: 4-Star Pool Villa on a Rocky Cape
entries.name: Captain Hook Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Yai Ki · near Klong Rahan (Secret Beach) · Koh Kood
tags: 🪨 Pool villas on a rocky cape
entries.addr: 15/9 Moo 4, Ao Yai Ki, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Captain Hook Resort is a pool-villa resort on a private rocky cape with two small beaches of its own, near Klong Rahan (Secret Beach), scoring 8.8 from 59 reviews. What reviews love is the extreme privacy — you arrive by longtail boat, so it feels like having your own island — with a canal to kayak and free kayaks, SUP and snorkel gear. A fit for couples or anyone wanting to cut off from the crowds, as long as you're fine with a more adventurous trip in and out.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: You come and go by boat, so check the boat times with the resort before planning trips to other bays. The Mini Pool Villa is only a little more and gives you a small private pool — worth it for couples.
pros: Private rocky cape with two small beaches of its own
Very private — feels like your own island
Free kayaks, SUP and snorkel gear
Pool villas with private pools to choose from
cons: You come and go by longtail boat — more adventurous than most
Hard to pop out to other bays — you depend on the boat times

entries.name: Tolani Resort Koh Kood
entries.addr: 43/8 Moo 2, Baan Klong Chao, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Tolani Resort is a boutique boho-natural villa resort on Klong Chao beach, scoring 8.4 from 46 reviews. The selling point is the natural-toned timber design that photographs beautifully, with everything from hillside sea-view villas to beachfront pool villas. It's on Klong Chao with white sand, clear water and restaurants nearby, plus free kayaks — a fit for anyone who loves a boutique look and design over a full set of facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Superior Seaview Villa is on a hill so you walk up, but it's well priced with a lovely view. If your budget stretches and you want true beachfront, pick a Beachfront Villa.
pros: Boho-natural design, photogenic decor
On Klong Chao beach — white sand, clear water
Range of rooms from hillside view to beachfront pool villa
Free kayaks to borrow
cons: Scores a touch lower than its 4-star neighbours
Hillside villas mean stairs — not ideal if walking is hard

entries.name: The Little White Bird Traveller Hostel
tags: 🛶 Free kayaks · share Peter Pan's beach
entries.addr: 43/16 Moo 2, Baan Klong Chao, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Little White Bird is a white-toned minimal hostel from the Captain Hook Group scoring a high 9.6. Although it's a 1-star stay, the rooms are private with air-con and en-suite bathrooms — not shared dorm beds like a typical hostel. Reviews love the lovely staff, free breakfast, a 24-hour shared kitchen and free kayaks, and guests can use the beach at sister property Peter Pan. It's the cheapest pick in the Klong Chao area for travellers who want good vibes on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The River View room overlooking the Klong Chao canal has the best vibe for only a little more. The hostel isn't right on the beach, but you can walk to sister property Peter Pan's beach — just allow a little walking time.
pros: High-scoring hostel at 9.6 · private rooms with AC and en-suite
Free breakfast, 24h shared kitchen
Lovely staff · free kayaks to borrow
Cheapest in the Klong Chao area, use Peter Pan's beach
cons: Not on the beach — you walk to the sister property's beach
A simple stay with none of the resort-style facilities

entries.name: Koh Kood Garden
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Klong Mad · near Ao Tapao · Koh Kood
entries.addr: Klong Mad, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Koh Kood Garden is the cheapest stay in this guide — from just ฿1,200 — scoring 8.4 from 40 reviews. It's a set of small air-con bungalows in a garden amid the forest in the Klong Mad area, run hands-on by the owner, with a simple, quiet back-to-nature feel. It's not on the beach but it's near Ao Tapao — a fit for budget travellers who'll rent a scooter and explore the island themselves. Rooms range from doubles to family bungalows and whole-house rental for groups.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's not on the beach, so renting a scooter to get around the island is the most convenient way to stay here. Booking direct with the property can sometimes get a better rate, since the listings on the major booking sites aren't always stable.
pros: Cheapest in this guide — from ฿1,200
Air-con garden bungalows, quiet and back-to-nature
Hands-on owner, friendly atmosphere
Family rooms and whole-house rental for groups
cons: Not on the beach — you'll need to rent a scooter to get around
Simple bungalows with none of the resort-style facilities

entries.name: Rest Sea Resort Koh Kood
entries.addr: 134 Moo 2, Ao Phrao, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Rest Sea Resort is a minimal boutique villa resort on Ao Phrao beach at the south tip of the island, scoring 8.1 from 26 reviews. The villas are minimal-design, around 25 sqm, ranging from garden villas to tiny-pool villas and beachfront villas. The starting price is friendly at ฿2,600, with free kayaks and SUP. It's down at the south tip — fairly far and quiet — a fit for anyone wanting to cut off from the bustle, as long as you allow travel time to the other bays.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ao Phrao is at the south tip and the final stretch of road climbs hills — allow time and check the route with the resort. Step up to a Deluxe Pool Villa for an affordable tiny private pool.
pros: Minimal-design villas, friendly starting price
Tiny private-pool villas at an affordable rate
Down at the south tip — quiet and private
Free kayaks and SUP to borrow
cons: Still few reviews (26), score below the island average
At the south tip, far from the other bays — long travel on the island

entries.name: Ko Kut Ao Phrao Beach Resort

rooms.type: Sea Breeze Hut (by the sea, sunset view)

entries.addr: 62 Moo 5, Ao Phrao, Ko Kut · Koh Kood, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Ko Kut Ao Phrao Beach Resort is a budget beachfront resort on Ao Phrao, where the shallow water is great for families with kids, scoring 8.0 from 36 reviews. It has garden rooms, seaside bungalows, and a Family Hut for 4. The highlights are the safe shallow beach for kids, a wooden jetty for the sunset and free kayaks. From ฿1,800 it's a budget pick for families who want to be on the beach, though it's at the south tip, so allow travel time.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a family, the Family Hut is better value. Ao Phrao's shallow water is great for kids to wade in, but at very low tide it can be too shallow to swim — check the tide times.
pros: Safe shallow beach — great for families with kids
Has a Family Hut for 4, budget price
Wooden jetty for lovely sunsets, free kayaks
Friendly starting price for a beachfront resort
cons: Lowest score in this guide, simple facilities
At the south tip, far from the other bays — long travel on the island

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates and may change by date and season — always check the live price and compare 3 sites before booking. Koh Kood room rates swing a lot by season: in high season (November–April · especially New Year, Songkran and long weekends) prices rise and rooms sell out fast, so book 1–2 months ahead. In low season (May–October) the sea is rough and many resorts close — confirm the open/close dates before booking. Koh Kood has no public transport; get around the island by rented scooter, songthaew or your resort's shuttle. Reach the island by speedboat from Laem Sok / Laem Ngop pier in Trat, about 1–1.5 hours. Scores and highlights come from reading real guest reviews; we did not stay ourselves. Article by ThailandAddict
faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Koh Kood hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which bay is best to stay on Koh Kood?
faq.a: It depends on your style. Klong Chao suits anyone wanting lots of stays and restaurants — a long white-sand beach with a kayak canal (Tinkerbell, Tolani, Peter Pan, Little White Bird). Bang Bao is a clear-water curved bay in the south, quiet and pretty (The Beach Natural). Ao Tapao is a calm hilltop with sea views, good for couples (Shantaa). Ao Phrao / Klong Mad / Ao Ngamkho are quiet private beaches and mid-island locations (Koh Kood Beach Resort, Dusita, Rest Sea, Ao Phrao Beach Resort).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Koh Kood hotels cost?
faq.a: Quite a range: garden bungalows and hostels start around ฿1,200–2,600 per night; mid-range and 3-star beachfront resorts around ฿2,400–4,500; 4-star villas and beachfront resorts from ฿4,500–7,000+, and front-row beachfront pool villas can run into five figures. Rates swing a lot by season — high season (New Year, Songkran, long weekends) can be much higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Kood — which pier?
faq.a: Koh Kood is at the far end of the Trat sea, so you take a speedboat from Laem Sok or Laem Ngop pier in Trat, about 1–1.5 hours. Most people buy a van-from-Bangkok plus boat package, or drive themselves and park at the pier. Many resorts run their own boat and shuttle service — just ask when booking. Check the boat times ahead, as there are limited departures per day.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get around Koh Kood?
faq.a: Koh Kood is a large island with no public transport, and the bays are far apart. The popular options are renting a scooter to explore yourself (some stretches climb steep hills, so ride carefully) or chartering a songthaew. Many resorts have airport/boat transfers and can take you to sights. If you stay in a far bay like Ao Phrao or Bang Bao, having a private vehicle or rented scooter is more convenient.

faq.q: ❓ When should you visit Koh Kood — does low season close?
faq.a: The best time is November–April, with clear water, good weather and sunshine — that's high season. May–October is low season, with lots of rain, rough seas and many resorts closed, so always check the property's open/close dates before booking. Over New Year, Songkran and long weekends rooms sell out fast and prices are high, so book 1–2 months ahead.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest to book a Koh Kood hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so open all three to compare before booking — every review page in this guide has price-compare links. Some small island resorts give a better rate when you book direct, and you can ask about boat transfers at the same time.
